# ui::ContextMenuHost

Header: `winui/render/ContextMenuHost.hpp`.

Shows a context menu drawn by the system on a control's behalf.

Call it from [Element::handle_context_menu()](../tree/element.md#handle_context_menu). The library implements it, and a test installs TestContextMenuHost.

A control doesn't draw its right-click menu itself. It builds a flat item list and calls [show()](#show), and the window shows it as a system menu, with the system's theming, keyboard navigation and screen-reader support. [Window](../tree/window.md) passes the host into [Element::handle_context_menu()](../tree/element.md#handle_context_menu), the only moment a control may show a menu, so don't keep it.

Example: 
```cpp
class MyEditor : public ui::Element
{
public:
    bool handle_context_menu(std::optional<ui::Point> position, ui::ContextMenuHost& host) override
    {
        const ui::Point at = position.value_or(caret_point()); // keyboard request: own anchor
        const std::vector<ui::ContextMenuItem> items{
            {"Cut"}, {"Copy"}, ui::ContextMenuItem::separator(), {"Paste"}};
        if (const std::optional<std::size_t> picked = host.show(at, items))
        {
            run_command(*picked); // 0 = Cut, 1 = Copy, 3 = Paste
        }
        return true; // a menu was shown, even if dismissed
    }

private:
    ui::Point caret_point() const;
    void      run_command(std::size_t index);
};
```

## ~ContextMenuHost

```cpp
virtual ~ContextMenuHost() = default
```

## show

```cpp
virtual std::optional<std::size_t> show(Point position, const std::vector<ContextMenuItem>& items) = 0
```

Shows `items` as a popup menu whose top-left corner sits at `position` (window-client DIPs, the same space [Element::bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) uses), blocks until the user picks an item or dismisses the menu, and returns the picked item's index into `items`, or nullopt on dismissal. Separators and disabled items are never returned.
